title: Quality-first small-batch regional capacity worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This working worksheet explores a quality-first approach to quantization + small-batch sizing for regionally distributed GPU fleets. The goal: keep conversational and classification quality loss under an explicit budget while recovering as much throughput as possible through quantization and micro-batching. This is intentionally a conservative planning artifact for teams owning low-latency customer-facing routes (chat/assistant + strict hallucination constraints).

Assumptions & definitions:
- Reference models: open-vicuna-13B (decoder), redwood-chat-7B-rc1 (chat), classification-distill-3B.
- GPU types considered: H100-80GB, A100-80GB, L4-48GB (edge region).
- Quant levels: fp16 (baseline), int8, int4 (8-bit and 4-bit simulated via quant toolchain), and experimental 3-bit (lossy research).
- Batch sizing: small-batch (1-8 tokens/requests multiplexed), microbatching (internal batching at token-level; exposed as batch_size param).
- Quality metrics: classification accuracy (ACC), rouge-L (summarization), BLEU for short-form generation, hallucination rate (HR) measured by eval suite.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 280ms for local region chat routes; global-fallback routes p95 < 400ms.

Empirical baseline numbers (measured on staging H100 pool):
- Baseline per-GPU sustained throughput (fp16, batch=1, avg seq_len=128): 28k tokens/s (vicuna-13B on H100).
- int8 speedup multiplier vs fp16: 1.35x (measured); int4: 1.9x; 3-bit: 2.4x (research, unstable).
- Quality deltas (relative to fp16 baseline):
  - int8: ACC -0.6% absolute, rouge-L -0.8 pts, HR +0.7ppt
  - int4: ACC -1.9% abs, rouge-L -2.6 pts, HR +2.4ppt
  - 3-bit: ACC -4.5% abs, rouge-L -6.8 pts, HR +6.1ppt
- Latency impact of batching: per-request p95 increases with batch size; observed p95 penalty = base_latency + 8ms * (batch_size - 1) for batch<=8 on H100.

Throughput model (conservative):
effective_tokens_per_gpu = baseline_fp16_tokens * quant_speedup * batch_scale * (1 - overhead_pct)
where:
- baseline_fp16_tokens: 28k for vicuna-13B H100 (scale down for A100/L4 by 0.85/0.45 respectively)
- quant_speedup: int8=1.35, int4=1.9, 3bit=2.4
- batch_scale: modest parallelism wins for batch>1, use batch_scale = 1 + 0.05*(batch_size-1) (small-batch diminishing returns)
- overhead_pct: network + scheduling overhead, conservatively 6% for regional, 12% for cross-region fallbacks

Quick reference table (vicuna-13B, avg seq=128):
- H100 fp16 batch1: 28k t/s, p95 210ms, quality baseline
- H100 int8 batch2: ~28k * 1.35 * 1.05 * (1-0.06) ≈ 39.3k t/s, p95 ≈ 226ms, quality: -0.6% ACC
- H100 int4 batch4: ~28k * 1.9 * 1.15 * (1-0.06) ≈ 57.3k t/s, p95 ≈ 242ms, quality: -1.9% ACC
- A100 fp16 batch1: 28k * 0.85 ≈ 23.8k t/s
- L4 int8 batch2 (edge): 28k * 0.45 * 1.35 * 1.05 * (1-0.06) ≈ 8.4k t/s (note memory constraints limit seq length)

Quality-first regional scenarios (target p95 <= 280ms, ARRiving traffic = 1.2B tokens/day global):
Scenario A (conservative high-quality): prefer int8 + batch1-2 in primary regions, avoid int4 on chat routes.
- Traffic split (expected): us-west 40%, us-east 30%, eu-west 20%, apac-sg 10%
- Daily tokens by region: us-west 480M, us-east 360M, eu-west 240M, apac-sg 120M
- Required sustained tokens/s by region (24h): us-west 5.56k t/s, us-east 4.17k t/s, eu-west 2.78k t/s, apac-sg 1.39k t/s
- Using H100 int8 batch2 (39.3k t/s effective): GPUs needed = ceil(required_t/s / 39.3k) => us-west 1, us-east 1, eu-west 1, apac-sg 1 (capacity headroom recommended x1.6). With headroom, plan: us-west 2 H100, us-east 2 H100, eu-west 1 H100 + 1 A100, apac-sg 1 A100 or 2 L4s for burst.
- Risk: int8 ACC delta -0.6% absolute; still within quality budget for customer-facing assistant.

Scenario B (throughput-lean within quality budget): allow int4 for background summarization routes only; chat routes stay int8 or fp16.
- Strategy: split routes per model instance labels: chat-prefixed servers enforce quant>=int8; summarization and long-form pipelines can use int4 with larger batches.
- Example capacity math (chat routes only, us-west chat load 60% of region tokens): us-west chat 2.78k t/s required. On H100 int8 batch2 (39.3k t/s), one GPU handles chat and leaves leftover capacity for background tasks; background summarization can be scheduled on int4 slots to increase total region throughput by ~45% but must be isolated by routing policy.

Cost/quality sensitivity matrix (rules of thumb):
- Small per-route quality budget (<=1% ACC drop): prefer int8, small-batch (1-2), restrict int4 to non-critical routes.
- Moderate budget (1-3% ACC drop): int4 acceptable for long-form, high-seq workloads with batch 2-4 and strong eval suites.
- Aggressive budget (>3% ACC drop allowed): experimental low-bit or 3-bit for offline workloads only.

Headroom / overprovision guidance:
- Always target 1.4–1.8x steady-state headroom for primary regions with traffic spikes and failover absorbance. For apac/low-traffic regions target 1.2–1.5x depending on burst SLA.
- Reserve a 10% slot pool (warm idle GPUs) per region for canary/rollouts to avoid cross-region cold-starts.

Operational notes (action items):
1) Add region-specific quant profiles to model catalog: label models as {fp16,int8,int4} and tag route safety-critical=true/false. (Owner: Rahul)
2) Implement routing policy changes: allow per-route quant minimum and denylist int4 for safety-critical routes. (Owner: Elena)
3) Build a small-batch capacity simulator (inputs: per-route token distribution, seq length histogram, quant profile, batch limits) to produce per-region GPU counts and p95 predictions. Target prototype: 2 weeks. (Owner: Maya)
4) Run degraded-quality evals for int4 on our hallucination suite and a user-facing A/B on 5% traffic in staging (stop if HR increases >2ppt). (Owner: SRE + Applied ML)
5) Create a dashboard widget in Console showing per-route quant profile, observed quality drift (daily), and GPU-utilization vs effective-throughput. (Owner: Observability)

Open questions & unknowns:
- Int4 stability on long chat sessions (seq >1024) — memory fragmentation on L4 observed, unknown for future microkernel patches.
- Cross-region fallback overhead modeling for prefix caching (we use 12% cross-region overhead here; need refined telemetry).
- Fine-grained cost tradeoffs when mixing A100/H100/L4; TCO model needs more accurate spot pricing and committed-reserve effects.

Appendix: quick calc examples
- How many H100s for a route needing 10k t/s on avg (p95 budget 280ms): using int8 batch2 effective 39.3k t/s -> 1 GPU suffices; with 1.6x headroom -> 2 GPUs (warm+active).
- If we switch to int4 batch4 effective 57.3k t/s -> 1 GPU with larger headroom, but verify quality on eval suite first.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a conservative planning worksheet targeted at product teams who cannot accept >1.5% quality regression on chat. Numbers are intentionally rounded and should be validated with the small-batch simulator called out in action item #3.
- Please comment with region-specific traffic multipliers or local pricing estimates.
